newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY NOON RADIO HEADLINES - MARCH 17.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY NOON RADIO HEADLINES - MARCH 17.

text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:
- Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus will negotiate with Hungarian politicians about economic matters on Monday.
- Jozsef Torgyan, President of the opposition Smallholder's Party (FKGP) said his party supported the demonstrations of farmers as agricultural interest groups were too weak in Hungary.
- Trade unions of employees in higher education set up a strike committee, preparing for a possible demonstration over the delay in wage hikes due this month.

- Small investors of Port Rt, a subsidiary of C-Nexus Rt which is under liquidation, said they would demonstrate at the Parliament if they will not get back their money, totalling one billion forints.
- A man, whose child died of lead-poisoning, was found guilty by the court, but only of damaging the environment.
